For example an imp-ring with\nthree points and three processes running in this sequence:\n\n\n    impsize   equ 2667                 ; (CORESIZE+1)/3\n\n    a         mov   0, impsize         ; copy self to b\n    b         mov   0, impsize         ; copy self to c\n    c         mov   0, impsize         ; copy self to a+1\n\n\nOne method of launching an imp-ring:\n\n\n    impsize   equ 2667\n\n    example   spl   impsize+1\n              mov   example, impsize\n    imp       mov   0, impsize\n\n\n\n\n\n\nImp-Spiral\n\nAn imp-like program with multiple\nprocesses supporting each other. For example a three-point spiral,\nwith six processes running in this sequence: \n\n\n    impsize   equ 2667                 ; (CORESIZE+1)/3\n\n    a         mov   0, impsize         ; copy self to b\n    b         mov   0, impsize         ; copy self to c\n    c         mov   0, impsize         ; copy self to a+1\n    a+1       mov   0, impsize         ; copy self to b+1\n    b+1       mov   0, impsize         ; copy self to c+1\n    c+1       mov   0, impsize         ; copy self to a+2\n\n\nSee binary launch,\nJMP/ADD launch\nand vector launch for examples of launching imp-spirals.\n\n\n\n\nIncendiary Bomb\n\nA type of stun bomb which creates a SPL\n0 carpet. \n\n\n    example   spl   0, 8\n              mov   example, &lt;example\n\n\nModern incendiary bombs use separate SPL /\nMOV bombs:\n\n\n    sp        spl   0, sm+1            ; spl half of the incendiary\n\n              ...\n\n    sm        mov   sp, >sp            ; mov half of the incendiary\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\nJMP/<code\nclass=\"code88\">ADD Launch\n\nOne of several means to start an \nimp-spiral running. The slowest launch technique, but requires\nthe least code. See also binary launch\nand vector launch. \n\n\n    impsize   equ 2667\n\n    example   spl   1                  ; extend by adding more spl 1's\n              spl   1\n              spl   2\n              jmp   @0, imp\n              add   #impsize, -1       ; bump address by impsize after each jmp\n              dat   #0, #0             ; excess processes must die!\n    imp       mov   0, impsize         ; in '94 use -&gt; mov.i #0,IMPSIZE\n\n","metadata":{"output":"\n\n\n\nImp-Ring\n\nA minimal imp-spiral. It ignores hits on its own code using a range check with `slt`, and stops scanning after 800 tries.\n- On the first real hit it drops `jmp 0` bombs on both cells, moves the clear's pointer to the hit, and runs a `spl #0` / `dat` core-clear forward from the enemy.\n\nWhat made the difference:\n- **Distance between the two compared cells:** this mattered most. In the first round, P-cell 0 is\n--\n420-       result.\n421-\n422:       There are two new instructions for accessing P-space:\n423-\n424:       LDP    (Load P-space) loads P-space cell specified by A-value into core\n425-              at B-address.\n426-\n427:       STP    (Store P-space) stores A-value into P-space cell specified by B-\n428-              value.\n429-\n430:       It is important to note that P-space cells are refered to by A/B-values\n431-       as opposed to A/B-addresses. As an example, \"STP #9,#1\" stores number 9\n432-       in P-cell 1.\n433-\n434:       Since  all  P-space access is only via these two instructions, it takes\n435:       too much time and space to use P-space for working variables where they\n436:       would  be safe from the opposing warrior. P-space was made deliberately\n437-       hard to access, unlike a set of general purpose registers.\n438-\n439:       P-space can also be used for communication between  warriors  belonging\n440:       to  a  team  in multi-warrior core war. To allow communication, P-space\n441-       has to be declared as \"shared\".  You  do  this  by  including  the  PIN\n442-       pseudo-opcode in your source:\n443-\n444:       PIN    (P-space Identification Number) has a single numerical argument.\n445-              If two or more participating warriors have the  same  PIN  argu-\n446:              ment,  they  share the same P-space. If the PIN pseudo-opcode is\n447:              missing from a warrior's source, its P-space  is  strictly  pri-\n448-              vate. {"type":"text","timestamp":1794664216193,"sessionID":"ses_e25c3473dffeBu4mTZaDb6gC4F","part":{"id":"prt_1da52b677001OqMaCnLtC7gpt1","messageID":"msg_1da528e39001ZYp2GIWPcB5Tm5","sessionID":"ses_e25c3473dffeBu4mTZaDb6gC4F","type":"text","text":"I've submitted **\"Paper Pebble Spiral\"**. It scored a mean of **0.388** over 500 rounds against the 30 sparring warriors, where Dwarf scores 0.175.\n\n**What it does:** it splits its processes three ways and runs three strategies at once:\n- **A self-copying \"paper\":** three copying stages, each sending a copy to a different distance (3728, 5430 and 3423), with 8 processes. It also drops bombs aimed at imps.\n- **A bomber:** it spawns extra processes and drops two bombs every four instructions, with a step of 7019.\n- **An imp spiral:** 8 processes, launched by the standard JMP/ADD method.\n\n**How it compares:**\n\n| Warrior | Sparring score (mean) |\n|---|---|\n| My first bomber alone | ~0.33 |\n| Bomber + imp spiral | ~0.345 |\n| Submitted three-part warrior | 0.388 |\n| A separate scanner design | 0.390 |\n\nThe scanner was no better on average, and its worst matchups were much worse (0.085 against 0.187). Against the seven test warriors I wrote myself, the submitted one lost 1 round in 1,400; the scanner lost 540. That is why I chose it.\n\n**Tried and dropped (all scored worse):**\n- A short scan for the opponent before starting.\n- Running the paper and bomber without the imps, or with more imp processes.\n- Random copy distances (about 0.36).\n- Switching strategy between rounds using the persistent memory (p-space), on losses or by trying each strategy and keeping the better one: 0.30–0.36.\n\n**Caveats:**\n- **Noise:** pMARS sets starting positions from the source text, so any edit reshuffles them. Differences of about ±0.01 between versions are noise.\n- **Possible overfitting:** the tuned copy distances beat random ones by about 0.03 on the sparring set. That gain may not fully carry over to the hidden hill.\n- **Projected reward:** Dwarf scores a bit higher on the sparring set (0.175) than on the hill (0.1475). If that gap holds, the hill score might be roughly 0.33–0.36, a reward of about 0.55–0.6. That is only an estimate.","time":{"start":1794664216183,"end":1794664216188}}}
